name: Pendlay Row
description: The Pendlay row is a strict barbell rowing variation where the bar returns to the floor between every repetition. The dead-stop start eliminates momentum and forces a more explosive concentric contraction of the upper back musculature. With the torso held parallel to the floor, the rhomboids, middle and lower trapezius, and latissimus dorsi are heavily loaded through a full range of motion.

execution.starting_position: Stand over a barbell with feet hip-width apart and the bar over mid-foot. Hinge to grip the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width. The torso must be parallel or near-parallel to the floor. The bar rests on the floor at the start of every rep.
execution.setup_instructions: Set up exactly as you would for a conventional deadlift but set the torso to horizontal. Use a pronated grip. Bumper plates are helpful so the bar drops safely to the floor each rep.
steps: Step 1: Begin with the bar on the floor, torso parallel to the ground, arms extended.
Step 2: Take a breath and brace the core hard.
Step 3: Explosively row the bar toward the lower chest or upper abdomen by driving the elbows up and back.
Step 4: At the top, squeeze the scapulae together fully.
Step 5: Lower the bar all the way to the floor in a controlled manner and allow it to come to a complete stop before the next rep.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before each rep. Exhale after the bar makes contact with the floor.
common_mistakes: Bouncing the bar off the floor instead of achieving a true dead stop
Raising the torso to assist the row, reducing back stimulus and stressing the lower back
Not reaching full scapular retraction at the top of each rep
safety_considerations: The strict horizontal torso position places significant demand on the erector spinae — do not perform when lower back is fatigued
Use bumper plates if possible to protect the floor and bar
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full dead-stop at the bottom to full scapular retraction at the top. No partial reps.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Explosive concentric (as fast as possible under control), controlled 2s eccentric, full stop between reps.
coaching_cues: Torso parallel to the floor the entire set — if it rises, the weight is too heavy
Think of the row as a 'jump' for your upper back
Every rep starts from zero — no rebound
